title: Hidden cross-project coupling: the root application probes runtime process names
affected_capabilities: Runtime census and atlas tooling, deployment model
evidence: lib/tiannara/crav/runtime_atlas.ex:582 and lib/tiannara/crav/runtime_census.ex:246 call Process.whereis(TiannaraRuntime.StartupSupervisor); lib/tiannara/phase_omega/runtime_auditor.ex:252 references TiannaraRuntime.Monitoring.TelemetryPublisher and lib/tiannara/phase_omega/runtime_discoverer.ex:151 uses Code.ensure_loaded?; all are guarded so there is no compile dependency and the root mix.exs has no runtime dependency, but they imply a co-VM deployment that no launcher, compose or k8s file provides

title: No rollback restores state and the CBAC gate and authority verifier are dead code

title: The federation quorum contradicts its own documented guarantee and votes are replayable
evidence: tiannara_runtime/lib/tiannara/phase14/federation_gateway.ex:6 documents Byzantine fault tolerance Q >= ceil(2/3 N) but :11 sets @quorum_fraction 0.667 and :34 and :48 compute trunc(total * 0.667), a floor, so N=1 yields quorum 0 and N=2 yields 1 of 2; :44-56 votes carry no instance identity and no dedup so one voter can vote repeatedly; certification/audit/PHASE_5F_STATUS_CORRECTION.md:129-136 (C-07) records the CRA supervisor as absent with partition, cross-node-authority, dedup, snapshot-consistency and budget-reconciliation scope entirely absent
root_cause: The quorum constant was transcribed as a fraction and applied with trunc; the Byzantine voter model was documented in prose and never implemented
remediation: Use ceil and express the quorum in votes rather than a fraction of members; require a per-instance identity and reject duplicate votes from the same instance
acceptance_criteria: A test proves a 2-node cluster cannot reach quorum with 1 vote and that a duplicate vote from one instance does not increment the count
blast_radius: Cross-node consensus, audit merkle root
notes: Related F-GOV-012 (Merkle root has no consumer).

title: Systemic test-versus-production mismatch through fabrication and mock or loaded conflation
affected_capabilities: OPC execution, CIS safety delivery, observability path, test gate integrity
evidence: (a) OPC execution fabricated outputs and was quarantined fail-closed (7855aa6d, C-04; opc/runtime/gpu_execution_bridge.ex:326-338 historic); (b) the CIS ExecutionController delivery path is log-only (wiring audit:49, C-10) so the safety chain is wired but effects are not delivered; (c) the API to observatory edge has a simulation fallback that fabricates data on outage (tiannara_api/routes/observatory.py:38,602,622); (d) the no_mocks lesson: :code.all_loaded() loaded is not active for mock observatories (certification/audit/TIANNARA_RUNTIME_TEST_INVENTORY.md:147, fixed by d4747586); (e) 6 quarantined runtime tests with recorded re-admission conditions

acceptance_criteria: No silent-simulation path remains on a production edge (grep for fallback keywords plus a route test), the CIS delivery contract is documented and tested, and the quarantine list stays visible with dates
blast_radius: OPC execution, CIS safety chain, observatory reporting, every test gate
notes: Root cause class: mock or stub data presented as runtime evidence. Related F-COG-101, F-COG-010, F-PLT-015 and F-WRD-007.

title: An approved constitutional amendment changes nothing and never reaches the effective constitution
evidence: lib/tiannara/council/amendment_engine.ex:251-253 apply_amendment/2 only bumps the version string and discards proposed_changes; :45 and :155-158 write the amended constitution into the engine private state while the effective constitution is ConstitutionRepository.current/0 read by Council.constitution/0 (council.ex:10), which the engine never touches; :142-160 approve requires only a bare human_id; :193 healthy? always returns true

title: The crash-injection chaos test is flaky and can kill the test process itself
evidence: test/tiannara/world/chaos/replay_determinism_chaos_test.exs:66 - 'crash during version creation leaves no partial state' terminates with '** (EXIT from #PID<0.4033.0>) killed'. Reproduced 3/3 in isolation on unmodified code (sha ca95773b) and it passes or fails depending on timing.
root_cause: The test injects a crash by killing a resolved process id; when the resolved pid belongs to the test process itself the injected kill terminates the test, so the outcome depends on process scheduling rather than on the behaviour under test.
remediation: Kill a dedicated, supervised child process (not a pid resolved from shared state), and assert the survivor state through the child. Until then the test is not a reliable signal and must not be counted as evidence either way.
acceptance_criteria: The chaos test runs 20 consecutive times with a stable outcome and never terminates the test process
blast_radius: root test suite reliability; any audit that cites this test as evidence
source_section: R1/Batch 1 step F-GOV-005 (discovered while validating the change)
notes: Discovered 2026-10-21 while validating F-GOV-005. It is NOT a regression of that change: it reproduces 3/3 on the unmodified code. Recorded so that a future run does not misread it as a new failure, and so that no closure claim cites it as evidence.
